why: A security firm with $270-385m CCTV revenue in a $1.9-2.3bn market (a 14-17% share) and 50-80 reps each bringing in $2.5-5m a year is high but believable for B2B systems sales.
Yearly swings in new-car sales from -9.2% to +13.8%, along with letter grades and 1-10 scores, are believable country market data.
A 42,000-person product trial is large but possible, and every score distribution in Exhibit 3 adds up to 100%.
A national furniture market of about EUR 26bn today, with online at EUR 3.1bn growing to EUR 6.2bn, is believable.
For a supermarket chain, 6,000-15,000 extra shoppers a day at $1.20-1.60 profit each, $12-25m upfront and a few hundred thousand dollars a month in running costs are believable.
Imprints with GBP 12-42m in book sales and marketing budgets of 5-15% of sales are believable for a publisher.
For an online travel site, 1,300-3,000 extra bookings a day at EUR 14-17 profit each and EUR 21-35m upfront investments are on the high side but within a plausible range.
Twelve accounts bringing in $1-20m each with 8-74 staff work out to about $100-270k of revenue per employee, which is normal for an ad agency.
83 florist hours for 101 bouquets and 415 hours for 434 bouquets (about 50-57 minutes each) are believable, and the February staffing (0.5 plus two trainees making 2.5) is consistent.
Orders of about EUR 53-62 each and first-year profits of EUR 0.9-28 per customer imply thin but possible online-retail margins for 420,000 registrants.
